title: Exercise therapy for back pain
what: Sessions with an instructor: exercises that strengthen your back and belly muscles and teach you to move correctly.
why: For neck or low back pain, after a flare-up, a disc herniation, or spine surgery, as your doctor prescribes.
duration: a session usually lasts 30 to 60 minutes; the course usually runs several weeks
tell_doctor: Where it hurts and what makes it worse
Any numbness or weakness in your arms or legs
Osteoporosis, heart disease, or high blood pressure

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Bring X-rays, MRI scans, and reports, if you have them. The instructor will choose exercises.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: A light meal 1 to 2 hours before the session.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Comfortable sportswear, and socks or clean shoes.

steps: The instructor asks about your pain and watches how you move
Exercises are shown, and your technique is checked
You do exercises lying, sitting, or standing, at your own pace
At the end, stretching and advice for home
feel: There should be no sharp pain during exercise. Tell the instructor right away
after: Do your home routine regularly, a little every day
Muscles may ache for 1 to 2 days after the first sessions
If the pain gets worse, discuss it with your doctor
red_flags: Numbness between the legs, bladder problems, or fast-growing leg weakness: call emergency services
Sudden severe pain after exercise: stop and see a doctor

faq.q: Can I exercise when my back hurts?
faq.a: During an acute flare-up, activity is usually limited. Your doctor will say when to start.

faq.q: How long until I see results?
faq.a: The first improvement usually shows after a few weeks of regular sessions.

reminders.text: Back exercise session tomorrow. Bring sportswear, water, and your scans if you have them.
